results.author: 智机玄同 发布于 2026年10月10日 3 分钟阅读
highlights:
JarvisLabs 提供按分钟 GPU VM、Templates、Serverless 与 Clusters。本文核对 2026 年 10 月新价格和暂停后的存储费用。

智机玄同发布于 2026年10月10日 3 分钟阅读

资料核查日期： 2026年10月10日。价格、库存和服务商规则可能变化，请以官方页面为准。

文章目录

2026 年 9 月 24 日，JarvisLabs 发布了一条容易漏看的价格更新。

H100 SXM、H200 SXM 和 RTX PRO 6000 的 On-Demand 新价格从 10 月 5 日生效。旧价格仍能出现在部分页面摘要里，但已经不适合当作当前新实例报价。

本站按生效日期使用新价，并把 Reserved 与 Spot 留在普通 Compare 之外。

## 四种运行方式

JarvisLabs 当前提供 On-Demand GPU VM、预装环境 Templates、Serverless 和 GPU Clusters。

VM 给完整 root 权限。Templates 更适合直接打开 JupyterLab、VS Code 或 SSH。Serverless 面向模型端点。Clusters 则服务更大的多节点任务。

同一张 GPU 在不同产品里的交付方式不同。本文的结构化报价只记录单 GPU On-Demand VM。

## 当前单 GPU On-Demand 价格

截至 2026-10-10，面向印度以外客户的公开 USD 价格如下。

| GPU | vCPU | RAM | USD / GPU 小时 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L4 24GB | 32 | 124GB | 0.44 |
| A100 80GB SXM | 16 | 112GB | 1.49 |
| RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition 96GB | 28 | 160GB | 2.19 |
| H100 SXM 80GB | 16 | 200GB | 3.49 |
| H200 SXM 141GB | 28 | 300GB | 4.59 |

价格按 GPU 小时展示，实例按分钟计费。

A100 40GB 仍有公开小时价，但官方当前租赁配置没有清楚标明本站需要的 form factor，所以没有强行映射到 PCIe 或 SXM canonical。

B200 当前为询价，也没有为了填表生成静态价格。

...

## Pause 后怎么收费

JarvisLabs 的实例可以 Pause 和 Resume。官方 FAQ 说明暂停后不再收 compute，但保留数据继续按存储计费。

当前存储公开价是 USD 0.10/GB-month。官方 FAQ 还给出按小时折算的存储说明。

如果只是停几天，Pause 很方便。如果确定长期不用，仍应检查保留的文件系统，不要只看 GPU 已暂停。

results.title: Where to Rent an RTX PRO 6000 at the Cheapest Price (Oct 2026)
results.author: GPUBank Research
highlights:
The RTX PRO 6000 is the professional Blackwell card that puts 96 GB of memory on a single PCIe board, and in October 2026 the hour sold under that name runs from a 33-cent interruptible bid to $5.50 per GPU on Azure, with GetDeploying's median across 165 on-demand configurations at $2.21 4. The spread is not noise. Each price buys a different machine, a different meter and a different promise about interruption, and it also buys one of three editions of the card that do not run at the same speed: a 600 W Workstation card, a 300 W Max-Q, or a passively cooled Server Edition with less memory bandwidth. A page that lines up those hours without saying which is which compares things that cannot be compared, so every row below says what the hour includes, how it is billed, the smallest unit you can rent and, where the provider says so, which edition you get.

We started from our own survey of 29 September 2026 and re-read every figure on 16 October 2026 on the provider's own page, or on Vast.ai's public offer search, which lists the live listings behind its marketplace. Figures we could only see on an aggregator are labelled as such with the aggregator named. More than one price in five had moved in two weeks: Runpod's Secure Cloud went from $2.09 to $2.49, Verda's on-demand hour from $1.96 to $2.30, Nebius switched its preemptible capacity to a floating spot price on 8 October, and Vast.ai's own pricing pages for all three editions showed no offers while its search returned 81 rentable listings 5 6 7 8 1. This page is published by GPUBank, a GPU cloud run by GPU Compute OÜ in Tallinn, so read our own entry with that in mind: it is measured on the same terms as every other offer, and the text says where a marketplace, a spot tier or another cloud beats it.

...

Above GPUBank's list price a group of European and US clouds sells dedicated single cards between $1.74 and $2.41: Nova Cloud at $1.74, UpCloud at $1.88, EcoHash at $1.89, Cloudzy at $1.93, Lyceum at $1.99, JarvisLabs at $2.19, Koyeb at $2.20 and Sesterce at $2.41, all from GetDeploying's crawl of 15 October, and Verda at $2.30 on its own page with 30 CPU threads and 90 GB of RAM per GPU 4 6 24. Massed Compute's own page lists the card at $2.19 with 16 vCPU, 144 GB of RAM and 725 GB of storage, and Exoscale sells it at $2.00 per GPU only as an eight-card node 25 4. Their case rests on something other than price: a specific European jurisdiction, card payment, or an existing account. On the spot side, Verda's interruptible instances cost $1.15 and its serverless containers $2.53, or $1.27 on spot, while CoreWeave sells 8-GPU Server Edition spot nodes at $9.56 an hour, $1.195 per GPU 6 18. CloudRift's own page quotes the card only reserved, $1.16 for a month and $1.10 for three, with on-demand capacity on request 26. The long-term reservations seen on aggregators, Leaseweb at $0.88 per GPU on a 2-GPU server for a month, Database Mart at $0.90 on a 24-month term and Utho at $1.18 on 36 months, need a quote before anyone plans around them 4.

...

A dedicated RTX PRO 6000 costs from about $0.95 to $2.50 per hour on demand at marketplaces and specialised clouds, and $3.36 to $5.50 per GPU at the hyperscalers. GetDeploying's crawl of 15 October 2026 put the median on-demand price at $2.21 across 165 configurations, with spot at $1.35 and reserved at $1.90 4. GPUBank's $1.15 all-in hour is about half that median 3. Spot capacity runs from Vast.ai's $0.33 bids to about $2.56 for AWS spot, and reservations from aggregator listings near $0.48 to $2.42 for Azure on three years. Always check what the hour includes: a GPU-only marketplace rate and an all-in machine price can differ by more than $0.30 an hour once disk and traffic are added, and a per-GPU figure taken from an 8-GPU node is only available if you rent all eight.

### 03 What is the RTX PRO 6000 spot price?

RTX PRO 6000 spot prices ran from $0.33 to about $2.56 per GPU-hour on 16 October 2026, depending on the provider and the unit rented. Vast.ai's interruptible minimum bids started at $0.33 on a Max-Q card, and an outbid instance is paused 1. GPUBank's interruptible tier costs $0.69 per GPU with five minutes of notice through the metadata endpoint, a webhook and the console, and a stop rather than a deletion 3. Nebius moved to dynamic spot pricing on 8 October with a floor of $0.79 that can change with capacity 7. Verda's spot instances cost $1.15, CoreWeave's 8-GPU Server Edition spot nodes work out to $1.195 or $1.386 per GPU, Google's g4-standard-48 about $1.71 and AWS's g7e.2xlarge about $2.56 6 18 16 27. Spot suits batch work such as video generation or checkpointed fine-tuning, not a production API.

...

results.title: Nebius switches preemptible GPUs to dynamic spot pricing
results.author: Saurabh Khatri
highlights:
Since October 8, 2026, Nebius preemptible GPU prices move with demand, up to every 15 minutes. An H100 starts from $0.79 per GPU-hour, capped one cent below on demand.

By Saurabh Khatri · Published Oct 18, 2026

Nebius stopped charging fixed prices for its preemptible GPU virtual machines on October 8, 2026. Since then, the price of a preemptible B300, B200, H200, H100 or RTX PRO 6000 moves with spare capacity and demand for that GPU type in that region. Nebius announced the change in a blog post on September 22, 2026.

## How the price moves

- The spot price can change as often as every 15 minutes.
- It stays between a floor and a ceiling. The ceiling is one cent below the current on-demand rate for the same GPU.
- The console shows the current price and up to 30 days of price history before you launch.
- The same spot price applies to preemptible capacity in Kubernetes clusters and Serverless AI.

## Old fixed prices and the new range

Per GPU-hour, in US dollars, excluding tax. The spot figures are the minimums that Nebius’s documentation lists; the ceiling follows from the one-cent rule and today’s on-demand prices.

| GPU | Fixed preemptible, before Oct 8 | Spot, from Oct 8 | Spot ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 | $4.30 | from $0.99 | $9.49 |
| B200 | $3.95 | from $0.99 | $8.49 |
| H200 | $2.45 | from $0.79 | $5.39 |
| H100 | $2.15 | from $0.79 | $4.49 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $0.95 | from $0.79 | $1.79 |

The floor is far below the old fixed prices, but the ceiling is close to the on-demand rate. What you pay depends on demand at the time. The L40S is not part of spot pricing and keeps a flat preemptible rate.

results.title: Hugging Face adds Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to Spaces from $2.75/hr — PricingSaaS Pulse
results.author: Rob Litterst
highlights:
# Hugging Face adds Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to Spaces from $2.75/hr

...

Published Oct 16, 2026

## What changed

Spaces hardware pricing gained four new Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 GPU options: 1x ($2.75/hr), 2x ($5.50/hr), 4x ($11.00/hr) and 8x ($22.00/hr). These are the same configurations and prices Hugging Face already offers on AWS Inference Endpoints. No existing hardware tier's price changed.

...

Spaces builders now get paid access to the same RTX PRO 6000 class of GPU Hugging Face already offers through Inference Endpoints, without moving the workload off Spaces. It continues a steady rollout of this GPU generation across the platform — Inference Endpoints in May, free Spaces GPUs in June, now paid Spaces hardware. Watch whether Hugging Face standardizes further, retiring older GPU options from Spaces hardware pricing as RTX PRO 6000 becomes the default rather than the newest add-on.

...

Hugging Face already sells this exact chip: the same four configurations and prices — 1x at $2.75/hr up to 8x at $22.00/hr — appeared on AWS Inference Endpoints on May 25, 2026, and free Spaces GPUs were upgraded to RTX Pro 6000 on Jun 1. Paid Spaces hardware now offers it too. Hugging Face has now made 9 tracked feature additions since granular Resource groups landed in Apr 2024, arriving just 8 days after it swapped PRO's 20x inference multiplier for a flat $2 monthly credit. Feature additions are a crowded category right now — MindsDB and Together shipped new capabilities the same day.

results.title: RTX PRO 6000 Price in 2026: Buy the Card or Rent It?
highlights:
The RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell doubled in price in about 17 months without a single hardware change. NVIDIA never announced the increases; the listing on its US Marketplace simply changed. Here is the sequence for the Workstation Edition, as tracked by Tom's Hardware:

1. March 2025: pre-orders briefly as low as $7,673, after the card was announced at NVIDIA GTC.
2. April 2025: the card goes on sale at $8,565 for a single unit and $8,435 for bulk orders.
3. June 2026: NVIDIA's Marketplace price rises to $13,250.
4. August 2026: it rises again, to $16,000, roughly 87% above the launch price.
